# MiniOneRec

<!-- Generated by `make minionerec` (ml/eval/minionerec.py). Do not edit by hand. -->

> **Preliminary.** The main run covers 434 of 4,866 test samples. Intervals are wide and the segment and paired results are indicative only; `make minionerec-gen` on the full test split replaces them.

MiniOneRec (generative retrieval: a Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct model fine-tuned to emit an
item's three-token semantic ID, decoded with beam search constrained to the catalog's
SIDs), run with its published Office checkpoint on this Mac's GPU, then scored on the
same split and with the same metric code as Pop, ItemCF and SASRec in
[offline.md](offline.md). The questions: does the published result reproduce, which
users does it help, and what does a request cost.

## Setup

|  |  |
|---|---|
| Checkpoint | MiniOneRec `Office_ckpt` (Hugging Face `kkknight/MiniOneRec` @ 365a03fc): Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct after SFT and GRPO, saved at RL step 1,038 of 3,456 (its trainer_state.json); bfloat16, 3.56 GB |
| Code | MiniOneRec's own `evaluate.py` (third_party/MiniOneRec @ 0cbd94de) with [a patch for Apple Silicon](../../minionerec/evaluate.py.patch): the device is `mps` when there is no CUDA, `import bitsandbytes` (CUDA-only, unused) is dropped, the model is loaded in a dtype and with an attention implementation given on the command line, and every batch is timed. Prompts, the SID prefix tree and the constrained beam search run as published. Shards: one (evaluate.sh runs 8, one per GPU). Attention: transformers' eager implementation. On MPS, PyTorch's scaled_dot_product_attention returns NaN for the pad rows of a left-padded batch, and the NaN spreads to the whole sample, which then decodes no SID (see `minionerec/upstream.py`) |
| Generation | 50 beams, all returned; batch 8; length penalty 0.0; at most 256 new tokens (evaluate.sh's settings) |
| Hardware | Apple M4 Pro, 16-core GPU, 24 GB unified memory, macOS-26.6.2-arm64-arm-64bit; device `mps`; PyTorch 2.6.0, transformers 4.57.1 (MiniOneRec's pinned versions); bfloat16, eager attention |
| Samples | 434 of 4,866 test samples: every sample of 200 random test users (seed 20261106) |
| Metrics | HR@K and NDCG@K, K = 3, 5, 10, as in offline.md. **Item rule** (main): a generated SID stands for every item that has it, in the tie order (training popularity, then item_id), so the 15 pairs of items that share a SID take two ranks; **SID rule**: the rank of the target's SID among the beams, which is what MiniOneRec's calc.py computes |
| Baselines | Pop, ItemCF and SASRec exactly as in offline.md (train rows only, tuned on validation), scored on the same samples |
| Intervals | 95%, user-level bootstrap: 1,000 replicates, seed 20261106; the same replicates for every model, so paired differences are comparable |

## Reproduction

MiniOneRec, arXiv:2510.24431v1, Table 1 (Office) reports MiniOneRec on this split, scored by its calc.py. The same
calc.py, unmodified, on our generations:

| Model | Metrics | HR@3 | HR@5 | HR@10 | NDCG@3 | NDCG@5 | NDCG@10 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Paper, Table 1: MiniOneRec | as reported | 0.1217 | 0.1420 | 0.1634 | 0.1088 | 0.1172 | 0.1242 |
| Our MPS generations | calc.py (its own code) | 0.1014 | 0.1129 | 0.1359 | 0.0874 | 0.0923 | 0.0996 |
| Our MPS generations | ours, SID rule | 0.1014 [0.0742, 0.1332] | 0.1129 [0.0831, 0.1458] | 0.1359 [0.1034, 0.1695] | 0.0874 [0.0627, 0.1155] | 0.0923 [0.0671, 0.1210] | 0.0996 [0.0751, 0.1291] |
| Our MPS generations | ours, item rule | 0.0991 [0.0739, 0.1290] | 0.1129 [0.0831, 0.1458] | 0.1359 [0.1034, 0.1695] | 0.0845 [0.0613, 0.1119] | 0.0905 [0.0659, 0.1193] | 0.0978 [0.0734, 0.1263] |

- On this subset calc.py differs from the paper by -0.0275 HR@10 and -0.0246 NDCG@10. A subset cannot confirm the reproduction: the paper's numbers are for the whole test split, and the interval here is several times wider.
- Constrained decoding: calc.py counted 0 generated SIDs that are not in the catalog (its CC; MiniOneRec's README asks to check that it is 0, since a non-zero count means the constraint did not hold).
- Cross-check: our SID-rule numbers equal calc.py's at every K it prints (K up to the beam width).
- Same samples, other hardware: MiniOneRec's evaluation runs bfloat16 on CUDA GPUs. Beam search keeps the 50 best partial SIDs at every step, so rounding differences can swap near-tied beams and move a target in or out of the top K.

## Which users it helps

Item rule, intervals from a user-level bootstrap inside each group (the same replicates
for every model of a group). The hypothesis was that semantic IDs, built from item text,
help most on long-tail targets and short histories; the segments test it:

- **History length**: 1-3 or 4-10 items before the target (the window is at most 10).
- **Target popularity**: head = the 20.9% of items with at least 15 training interactions (the top 20% by count, ties included; 60.5% of all training interactions); tail = the rest. 58 test targets never occur in training.
- **Target category**: level 2 of the Amazon category path (37 values, e.g. Paper, Printer Ink & Toner, Writing & Correction Supplies); cross-category = the target's category is not the category of any history item. 130 targets have no level-2 category and count as the category 'unknown'.
- **Target day**: reviewed on the same day as the last history item, or later (the split offline.md reports on).

Findings (HR@10, item rule; "significant" = the 95% interval excludes 0):

- **All samples**: MiniOneRec's HR@10 is not significantly different from SASRec's (-0.0092 [-0.0359, +0.0183]).
- **History length**: MiniOneRec - SASRec is +0.0000 [-0.0561, +0.0522] on 1-3 items and -0.0125 [-0.0438, +0.0173] on 4-10 items (1-3 items minus 4-10 items: +0.0125 [-0.0505, +0.0754]); the two groups do not differ significantly.
- **Target popularity**: MiniOneRec - SASRec is +0.0000 [-0.0481, +0.0529] on head and -0.0188 [-0.0457, +0.0047] on tail (head minus tail: +0.0188 [-0.0365, +0.0753]); the two groups do not differ significantly.
- **Target category**: MiniOneRec - SASRec is +0.0276 [+0.0000, +0.0583] on cross-category and -0.0461 [-0.0918, -0.0047] on same category (cross-category minus same category: +0.0737 [+0.0234, +0.1237]); the difference is significantly larger on cross-category.
- **Target day**: MiniOneRec - SASRec is -0.0151 [-0.0594, +0.0254] on same day and -0.0043 [-0.0377, +0.0333] on later day (same day minus later day: -0.0108 [-0.0671, +0.0496]); the two groups do not differ significantly.

## Cost

The main run generated 434 samples in 26 min at 50 beams and batch 8: 3.57 s per sample, i.e. 59 min of this Mac's GPU per 1,000 recommendations (a test sample is one request); peak memory footprint 16.2 GiB. The 1-minute load average was at most 1.5 when a shard started. At this speed the full test split (4,866 samples as evaluate.sh's 8 shards, 13 s of start-up and model loading each) takes about 4.9 h.

Latency, throughput and memory per beam width have not been measured yet (`make minionerec-cost`, on an idle machine).
